notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable code strings: Reject invalid billing input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors, reusing existing codes like invalid_state and negative_amount rather than inventing new exception types.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0008] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per finance policy FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given. Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Use to_money and ZERO from ledgerly.money: In ledgerly/invoice.py, coerce unit prices with to_money() and seed sums with ZERO from ledgerly.money, mirroring line_total and invoice_total.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0004] Exclude bool when validating integers: When validating an integer argument, check isinstance(x, bool) first because bool is a subclass of int; otherwise True/False pass as quantities.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: Normalize every incoming datetime with `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` before comparing or doing arithmetic, as `ledgerly.subscriptions.current_period` does for both `at` and `sub.started_at`.
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
